statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the returned vector r is exactly the strictly increasing list of all integers x such that left <= x <= right and x is self-dividing. A positive integer x is self-dividing when its standard decimal representation (with no leading zeros) contains no digit 0 and, for every decimal digit d occurring in that representation, x mod d = 0. Equivalently, r = [x_0, x_1, ..., x_{m-1}] where x_0 < x_1 < ... < x_{m-1} and {x_0, ..., x_{m-1}} = {x | left <= x <= right and x is self-dividing}.
preconditions: left and right are I64 values whose mathematical integer values satisfy 1 <= left <= right <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(r), the integer r[i] satisfies left <= r[i] <= right.
preconditions: left and right are I64 values whose mathematical integer values satisfy 1 <= left <= right <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(r), r[i] is positive and its standard decimal representation contains no digit 0.
preconditions: left and right are I64 values whose mathematical integer values satisfy 1 <= left <= right <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(r) and every decimal digit d such that d ≠ 0 and d occurs in the standard decimal representation of r[i], r[i] mod d = 0.
preconditions: left and right are I64 values whose mathematical integer values satisfy 1 <= left <= right <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer x such that left <= x <= right and x is self-dividing (positive, with no zero decimal digit, and divisible by each of its decimal digits), there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(r) and r[i] = x.
preconditions: left and right are I64 values whose mathematical integer values satisfy 1 <= left <= right <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if left = right, then: (a) if left is self-dividing, len(r) = 1 and r[0] = left; (b) if left is not self-dividing, len(r) = 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if 1 <= left <= right <= 9, then len(r) = right - left + 1 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(r), r[i] = left + i.
preconditions: left and right are I64 values whose mathematical integer values satisfy 1 <= left <= right <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= len(r) <= right - left + 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and len(r) > 0, r[0] is the least self-dividing integer in [left, right], and r[len(r) - 1] is the greatest self-dividing integer in [left, right].
preconditions: left and right are I64 values whose mathematical integer values satisfy 1 <= left <= right <= 10000.

statement: For every left and right satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail (no overflow, out-of-bounds access, panic, or other error).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exists an integer x with left <= x <= right that is self-dividing, then len(r) > 0 and there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that left <= r[i] <= right and r[i] is self-dividing.
preconditions: left and right are I64 values whose mathematical integer values satisfy 1 <= left <= right <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the call on (left, right) returns r and the call on (a, b) returns s, the vector s is exactly the subsequence of r consisting of all entries x with a <= x <= b, in the same order.
